Mean branch length per region and type (domesticate vs wild)

Plot within group mean

to_plot_long <- plot_data %>%
  select(-comparison) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c(branch_len_wild, branch_len_dom),
               names_to = "status", values_to = "branch_len") %>%
  mutate(status = recode(status,
                          branch_len_wild = "wild",
                          branch_len_dom  = "domesticate"))

plot1 <- ggplot(to_plot_long, aes(x = region, y = log(branch_len), fill = status)) +
  geom_violin()+
  theme_bw()+ 
  labs(y="log(branch length)")+
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5, hjust=1))+
  scale_fill_manual(values = unname(khroma::color("bright")(7))[c(5, 6)])+
  labs(x="Continent", fill="type",title="Mean branch length per region and pig type",subtitle = "bar represents within group mean")+
  stat_summary(
    fun = mean,
    geom = "crossbar",
    aes(group = status),
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.9),
    width = 0.8,
    color = "red",
    linewidth = 0.4,
    show.legend = FALSE
  )

plot2 <- ggplot(to_plot_long, aes(x = region, y = branch_len, fill = status)) +
  geom_violin()+
  theme_bw()+ 
  labs(y="branch length")+
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5, hjust=1))

plot1

plot2

# Wilcox test within each region (wild vs. domesticate, is there a sig. difference in branch length?) wilcox test (paired) to test within each region, if there is a difference between the wild and the domesticate

asia   <- plot_data %>% filter(region == "Asia")
europe <- plot_data %>% filter(region == "Europe")

wilcox.test(asia$branch_len_wild,   asia$branch_len_dom,   paired = TRUE)
## 
##  Wilcoxon signed rank test with continuity correction
## 
## data:  asia$branch_len_wild and asia$branch_len_dom
## V = 5835396, p-value < 2.2e-16
## alternative hypothesis: true location shift is not equal to 0
wilcox.test(europe$branch_len_wild, europe$branch_len_dom, paired = TRUE)
## 
##  Wilcoxon signed rank test with continuity correction
## 
## data:  europe$branch_len_wild and europe$branch_len_dom
## V = 4666045, p-value < 2.2e-16
## alternative hypothesis: true location shift is not equal to 0
mean(asia$branch_length_diff)
## [1] 0.04532744
mean(europe$branch_length_diff)
## [1] 0.003750594
mean(asia$branch_len_wild)
## [1] 0.08279642
mean(asia$branch_len_dom)
## [1] 0.03746898
mean(europe$branch_len_wild)
## [1] 0.04174277
mean(europe$branch_len_dom)
## [1] 0.03799218

In both cases, the branch length is significantly higher in the wild than in the domesticate. Confirm this by simply checking the mean per each group. The difference is more pronounced in Asia than in Europe

Optional bar plots to visualize the wilcox results

europe_count_wild_greater <- 0
europe_count_domesticate_greater <- 0
europe_count_equal <- 0

for (i in seq_along(europe$gene)){
  sign <- europe[i, 9]
  if (sign > 0) {
    europe_count_wild_greater <- europe_count_wild_greater + 1
  }
  if (sign < 0) {
    europe_count_domesticate_greater <- europe_count_domesticate_greater + 1
  }
  else {
    europe_count_equal <- europe_count_equal + 1
  }
}
asia_count_wild_greater <- 0
asia_count_domesticate_greater <- 0
asia_count_equal <- 0
for (i in seq_along(asia$gene)){
  sign <- asia[i, 9]
  if (sign > 0) {
    asia_count_wild_greater <- asia_count_wild_greater + 1
  }
  if (sign < 0) {
    asia_count_domesticate_greater <- asia_count_domesticate_greater + 1
  }
  else {
    asia_count_equal <- asia_count_equal + 1
  }
}
df_counts <- data.frame(
  region = c("Asia", "Europe"),
  wild_greater = c(asia_count_wild_greater, europe_count_wild_greater),
  equal = c(asia_count_equal, europe_count_equal),
  domesticate_greater = c(asia_count_domesticate_greater, europe_count_domesticate_greater))

df_counts_long <- df_counts %>% pivot_longer(cols = c(wild_greater,equal,domesticate_greater), names_to = "group", values_to = "count")

p_bar <- ggplot(df_counts_long, aes(x=region, y=count, fill=group))+

df_counts <- df_counts %>%

df_counts_long_prop <- df_counts %>%

Plots by gene

Chromosome

Plot by each gene. Now, instead of collapsing we want each gene as a single point, to see if there is a pattern between the genes affected by domestication in Asia and in Europe. Also, now our measure of interest is the log of the ratio between the wild and domesticate branch lenght. This is nice, because the log will be positive with the wild > domesticate, and negative when the wild < domesticate. Plot by chromosome.

Also, plot both the scatter plot and the rank of the genes, as a bar plot. Color them chromosome, to see if there is a chromosome that is contributing significantly to the pattern.

plot_data_summary <- plot_data %>%
  select(-c(branch_len_wild, branch_len_dom)) %>%
  group_by(gene, region, chromosome) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_branch_length_ratio      = mean(branch_length_ratio, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_branch_length_difference = mean(branch_length_diff, na.rm = TRUE),
    n      = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
    mutate(
      chromosome = as.numeric(str_split_i(chromosome, "_", 2)),
      chromosome = factor(chromosome, levels = sort(unique(chromosome))))

plot_data_summary_wide <- plot_data_summary %>% pivot_wider(names_from  = region,
                                                    values_from = c(mean_branch_length_ratio, mean_branch_length_difference, n)) %>% drop_na() %>%
  mutate(n=n_Europe+n_Asia,
         log_eu   = log(mean_branch_length_ratio_Europe),
         log_asia = log(mean_branch_length_ratio_Asia),
         quadrant = case_when(
           log_eu >  0 & log_asia >  0 ~ "Both Asia and Europe wild > domesticate",
           log_eu <= 0 & log_asia >  0 ~ "Asia only wild > domesticate",
           log_eu >  0 & log_asia <= 0 ~ "Europe only wild > domesticate",
           log_eu <= 0 & log_asia <= 0 ~ "Both Asia and Europe wild < domesticate"))

chrom_cols <- setNames(
  colour("discrete rainbow")(nlevels(plot_data_summary$chromosome)),
  levels(plot_data_summary$chromosome)
)

p_quad <- ggplot(plot_data_summary_wide, aes(x=log(mean_branch_length_ratio_Europe), y=log(mean_branch_length_ratio_Asia), color = chromosome))+
  geom_point()+
  theme_bw()+
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0)+
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0)+
  scale_color_manual(values = chrom_cols)

p_col <- ggplot(plot_data_summary,
       aes(x = reorder_within(gene, -mean_branch_length_ratio, region),
           y = log(mean_branch_length_ratio),
           fill = chromosome, color = chromosome)) +
  geom_col(width = 1, linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0) +
  facet_wrap(~region, scales = "free_x") +
  scale_x_reordered() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = chrom_cols) +
  scale_color_manual(values = chrom_cols) +
  labs(x = "Genes (ranked within region)") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_blank(),
        axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.major.x = element_blank())

p_col_by_chrom <- plot_data_summary %>%
  mutate(panel = paste(region, chromosome)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = reorder_within(gene, -mean_branch_length_ratio, panel),
             y = log(mean_branch_length_ratio),
             fill = chromosome, color = chromosome)) +
  geom_col(width = 1, linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0) +
  facet_wrap(region ~ chromosome, scales = "free_x") +
  scale_x_reordered() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = chrom_cols) +
  scale_color_manual(values = chrom_cols) +
  labs(x = "Genes (ranked within panel)") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_blank(),
        axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
        legend.position = "none")

ggsave(
    filename = paste0("plots/by_chromosome/quad_scatter.jpg"),
    plot = p_quad,
    width = 8,
    height = 4.5,
    limitsize = FALSE)

ggsave(
    filename = paste0("plots/by_chromosome/bar_rank.jpg"),
    plot = p_col,
    width = 12, height = 5, dpi = 300, limitsize = FALSE)

ggsave(
    filename = paste0("plots/by_chromosome/bar_rank_chrom.jpg"),
    plot = p_col_by_chrom,
    width = 12, height = 8, dpi = 300, limitsize = FALSE)

Family

plot_data_summary <- plot_data_summary %>% 
  mutate (gene = str_split_i(gene, "_", 3)) 

or_annotated <- or_annotated %>%
  mutate(in_results = as.character(gene) %in% unique(as.character(plot_data_summary$gene)))

length(unique(plot_data$gene))

nrow(or_annotated %>% filter(in_results == TRUE))

plot_data_summary_gene_family %>% filter(is.na(Family)) %>% pull(gene) %>% unique() %>% length()

plot_data_summary_gene_family <- plot_data_summary_gene_family %>% filter(is.na(Family)==FALSE)

plot_data_summary_gene_family$Family <-as.factor(plot_data_summary_gene_family$Family)

KW test for chromosome, family in each reiong (including post hoc Dunn/ wilcox tests)

Like the chromosome results, difficult to interpret the plots. We can do a KW to test whether or not there is a statistical difference between families, as well as chromosomes. Using slightly different datasets for both because there are some genes for which we have chromosome information but no family information.

europe_gene_family <- plot_data_summary_gene_family %>% filter(region=="Europe")
asia_gene_family <-   plot_data_summary_gene_family %>% filter(region=="Asia")

europe_length <-      plot_data_summary %>% filter(region == "Europe")
asia_length <-        plot_data_summary %>% filter(region == "Asia")

Europe KW tests:

KW_family_eur = kruskal.test(mean_branch_length_ratio ~ Family,
                    data = europe_gene_family)
print(KW_family_eur)
## 
##  Kruskal-Wallis rank sum test
## 
## data:  mean_branch_length_ratio by Family
## Kruskal-Wallis chi-squared = 22.034, df = 16, p-value = 0.1421
KW_chrom_Europe = kruskal.test(mean_branch_length_ratio ~ chromosome,
                    data = europe_length)
print(KW_chrom_Europe)
## 
##  Kruskal-Wallis rank sum test
## 
## data:  mean_branch_length_ratio by chromosome
## Kruskal-Wallis chi-squared = 12.533, df = 11, p-value = 0.3249

NO significant result for Europe, for either chromosome or family.

KW_family_asia = kruskal.test(mean_branch_length_ratio ~ Family,
                    data = asia_gene_family)
print(KW_family_asia)
## 
##  Kruskal-Wallis rank sum test
## 
## data:  mean_branch_length_ratio by Family
## Kruskal-Wallis chi-squared = 29.047, df = 15, p-value = 0.01586
KW_chrom_aisa = kruskal.test(mean_branch_length_ratio ~ chromosome,
                    data = asia_length)
print(KW_chrom_aisa)
## 
##  Kruskal-Wallis rank sum test
## 
## data:  mean_branch_length_ratio by chromosome
## Kruskal-Wallis chi-squared = 21.345, df = 10, p-value = 0.01881

In Asia, we do see a significant result for both family and chromosome.

Post hoc: both dunn and wilcox

dunn.test(asia_length$mean_branch_length_ratio, 
          asia_length$chromosome,
          method="bonferroni",
          kw=TRUE)
##   Kruskal-Wallis rank sum test
## 
## data: x and group
## Kruskal-Wallis chi-squared = 21.3449, df = 10, p-value = 0.02
## 
## 
##                     Dunn's Pairwise Comparison of x by group                    
##                                   (Bonferroni)                                  
## 
## Col Mean-│
## Row Mean │          1          2          3          4          5          6
## ─────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
##        2 │   1.271809
##          │     1.0000 
##          │
##        3 │  -0.248448  -0.612312
##          │     1.0000     1.0000 
##          │
##        4 │   1.197699   0.588323   0.826546
##          │     1.0000     1.0000     1.0000 
##          │
##        5 │  -0.375351  -1.612387   0.112194  -1.412587
##          │     1.0000     1.0000     1.0000     1.0000 
##          │
##        6 │   0.726068   0.381701   0.709868   0.071373   0.855193
##          │     1.0000     1.0000     1.0000     1.0000     1.0000 
##          │
##        7 │   2.644912   2.019401   1.256612   0.665710   2.856522   0.299427
##          │     0.2247     1.0000     1.0000     1.0000     0.1178     1.0000 
##          │
##        9 │  -0.683200  -2.221048   0.026558  -1.635167  -0.249558  -0.952758
##          │     1.0000     0.7246     1.0000     1.0000     1.0000     1.0000 
##          │
##       12 │   2.361535   1.779758   1.297450   0.739880   2.564361   0.371897
##          │     0.5005     1.0000     1.0000     1.0000     0.2843     1.0000 
##          │
##       13 │   0.249464  -0.669168   0.342799  -0.915314   0.550038  -0.603691
##          │     1.0000     1.0000     1.0000     1.0000     1.0000     1.0000 
##          │
##       18 │   1.000341   0.719818   0.952387   0.439761   1.106446   0.317462
##          │     1.0000     1.0000     1.0000     1.0000     1.0000     1.0000 
## Col Mean-│
## Row Mean │          7          9         12         13
## ─────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────
##        9 │  -3.323254
##          │     0.0245*
##          │
##       12 │   0.169905   2.894546
##          │     1.0000     0.1044 
##          │
##       13 │  -2.011952   0.802136  -1.900854
##          │     1.0000     1.0000     1.0000 
##          │
##       18 │   0.148556   1.187341   0.076131   0.896065
##          │     1.0000     1.0000     1.0000     1.0000 
## 
## FWER = 0.05
## Reject Ho if adjusted p ≤ FWER/2, where (unadjusted) p = Pr(Z ≥ |z|)
pairwise.wilcox.test(asia_length$mean_branch_length_ratio,
                     asia_length$chromosome, p.adjust.method = 'bonf')
## Warning in wilcox.test.default(xi, xj, paired = paired, ...): cannot compute
## exact p-value with ties
## Warning in wilcox.test.default(xi, xj, paired = paired, ...): cannot compute
## exact p-value with ties
## Warning in wilcox.test.default(xi, xj, paired = paired, ...): cannot compute
## exact p-value with ties
## Warning in wilcox.test.default(xi, xj, paired = paired, ...): cannot compute
## exact p-value with ties

IN PROGRESS – genes annotated by function

Okay. We think the family information is based on gene structure. Possibly metabolic pathway? But what we also have information on is the odorants associated with each gene. So, maybe we can investigate that information just for our genes of interest.

anotated_genes <- read.csv("gene_odor_annotations_with_descriptions(1).csv", header=TRUE)
plot_data_odorants <- plot_data_summary %>% inner_join(anotated_genes, by="gene")
## Warning in inner_join(., anotated_genes, by = "gene"): Detected an unexpected many-to-many relationship between `x` and `y`.
## ℹ Row 1 of `x` matches multiple rows in `y`.
## ℹ Row 1181 of `y` matches multiple rows in `x`.

##   "many-to-many"` to silence this warning.
#EXAMPLE OF WHAT THE DATA LOOK LIKE FOR ONE GENE.
sOR10A1 <- anotated_genes %>% filter(gene == "sOR10A1") %>% select(Species,chromosome,gene,Matched_Receptor,Sr..No,Recognized_odorants,Perceived_odor, Odorant)

We know in Asia, the two gene families wit the significant different are families 4 and 7. So, maybe we can pull out just the genes in those families in Asia.

genes_Asia_group_4 <- plot_data_summary_gene_family %>% filter(region == "Asia" & Family == "4") %>% pull(gene)
genes_Asia_group_7 <- plot_data_summary_gene_family %>% filter(region == "Asia" & Family == "7") %>% pull(gene)
anotated_genes_asia_4 <- anotated_genes %>% filter(gene %in% genes_Asia_group_4) %>% filter(str_detect(Species, "Asian") == TRUE)
anotated_genes_asia_7 <- anotated_genes %>% filter(gene %in% genes_Asia_group_7) %>% filter(str_detect(Species, "Asian") == TRUE)

Also curious, what genes make up the highest 10% in terms of wild evolution and highest 10% in terms of domesticate evolution for both Europe and Asia. And then do the same thing, to see what smells might be associated there.

ten_percent_europe <- quantile(europe_length$mean_branch_length_ratio, .1)
ninty_percent_europe <- quantile(europe_length$mean_branch_length_ratio, .9)

ten_percent_asia <- quantile(asia_length$mean_branch_length_ratio, .1)
ninty_percent_asia <- quantile(asia_length$mean_branch_length_ratio, .9)
europe_bottom_10 <- europe_length %>% filter(mean_branch_length_ratio <=ten_percent_europe) %>% pull(gene)
europe_top_10 <-    europe_length %>% filter(mean_branch_length_ratio >=ninty_percent_europe) %>% pull(gene)

asia_bottom_10 <- asia_length %>% filter(mean_branch_length_ratio <=ten_percent_asia) %>% pull(gene)
asia_top_10 <-    asia_length %>% filter(mean_branch_length_ratio >=ninty_percent_asia) %>% pull(gene)
anotated_genes_europe_domesticate_dominant <- anotated_genes %>% filter(gene %in% europe_bottom_10) %>% filter(str_detect(Species, "European") == TRUE)
anotated_genes_europe_wild_dominant <-        anotated_genes %>% filter(gene %in% europe_top_10)    %>% filter(str_detect(Species, "European") == TRUE)

anotated_genes_asian_domesticate_dominant <- anotated_genes %>% filter(gene %in% asia_bottom_10) %>% filter(str_detect(Species, "Asian") == TRUE)
anotated_genes_asian_wild_dominant <-        anotated_genes %>% filter(gene %in% asia_top_10)    %>% filter(str_detect(Species, "Asian") == TRUE)

Odorant work is still a work in progress!!!!

Regression through the origin on gene scatterplot

Figures for paper version 1:

Going back to our quadrant plot, we want to add a linear regression. Null hypothesis is slope=0, meaning points randomly scatter around the origin. Alternative hypothesis: there is a linear relationship between the genes that are domesticated in Europe and in Asia. That is to say, that knowing something about the relationship between the wild and the domesticate branch lenght in Europe predicts something about that same relationship in Aisa.

OPTIONAL non-origin forced model

model <- lm(log(mean_branch_length_ratio_Asia) ~ log(mean_branch_length_ratio_Europe), data = plot_data_summary_wide)
summary(model)
## 
## Call:
## lm(formula = log(mean_branch_length_ratio_Asia) ~ log(mean_branch_length_ratio_Europe), 
##     data = plot_data_summary_wide)
## 
## Residuals:
##     Min      1Q  Median      3Q     Max 
## -6.3968 -0.9291 -0.3260  1.0812  4.7142 
## 
## Coefficients:
##                                      Estimate Std. Error t value Pr(>|t|)    
## (Intercept)                           0.68424    0.09491   7.209 3.88e-12 ***
## log(mean_branch_length_ratio_Europe)  0.16855    0.07220   2.334   0.0202 *  
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
## 
## Residual standard error: 1.652 on 329 degrees of freedom
## Multiple R-squared:  0.0163, Adjusted R-squared:  0.01331 
## F-statistic:  5.45 on 1 and 329 DF,  p-value: 0.02017
sigma(model)
## [1] 1.65228
summary(model)$r.squared
## [1] 0.01629503

Now, for the model through the origin

model_origin <- lm(log(mean_branch_length_ratio_Asia) ~ 0 + log(mean_branch_length_ratio_Europe), data = plot_data_summary_wide)
summary(model_origin)
## 
## Call:
## lm(formula = log(mean_branch_length_ratio_Asia) ~ 0 + log(mean_branch_length_ratio_Europe), 
##     data = plot_data_summary_wide)
## 
## Residuals:
##     Min      1Q  Median      3Q     Max 
## -5.7212 -0.2980  0.3867  1.6314  5.4495 
## 
## Coefficients:
##                                      Estimate Std. Error t value Pr(>|t|)    
## log(mean_branch_length_ratio_Europe)  0.31973    0.07423   4.307 2.18e-05 ***
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
## 
## Residual standard error: 1.775 on 330 degrees of freedom
## Multiple R-squared:  0.05323,    Adjusted R-squared:  0.05036 
## F-statistic: 18.55 on 1 and 330 DF,  p-value: 2.184e-05
r2 <- summary(model_origin)$r.squared
p  <- summary(model_origin)$coefficients[1, 4]

To add the predictive line to the plot

predicted_df <- data.frame(asia_pred = predict(model_origin, plot_data_summary_wide), mean_branch_length_ratio_Europe=log(plot_data_summary_wide$mean_branch_length_ratio_Europe))
lab <- paste0("R² = ", signif(r2, 3), "\n",
              "p = ", format(signif(p, 3), scientific = TRUE))


scatted_regression <- ggplot(data = plot_data_summary_wide, aes(x = log(mean_branch_length_ratio_Europe), y = log(mean_branch_length_ratio_Asia), color=quadrant)) + 
  geom_point() +
  geom_line(color='red',data = predicted_df, aes(x=mean_branch_length_ratio_Europe, y=asia_pred))+
  theme_bw()+
  theme(legend.position="bottom")+
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0)+
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0)+
  labs(x="Europe: log(wild bl /domesticate bl)",y="Asia: log(wild bl /domesticate bl)", title = "Branch length ratio by gene and continent", subtitle = "linear model forced through the origin", color="")+
  annotate("text", x = -Inf, y = Inf, hjust = -0.1, vjust = 1.5,
           label = lab, size = 3)+
  scale_color_mediumcontrast(guide = guide_legend(nrow = 2))

ggsave(
  filename = paste0("for_paper_plots/scatter_regression.png"),
  plot = scatted_regression,
  width = 6,
  height = 6,
  limitsize = FALSE)
